blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Few-step distillation offers efficient generation with diffusion and flow models, but preserving quality with only a few sampling steps remains challenging. Distribution-matching methods via score distillation provide a strong foundation, yet they rely on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution. At intermediate generation steps in few-step sampling, student-score estimation can be difficult, and commonly used estimators may describe a different distribution from the one used to update the student. Flow matching allows a more flexible approach to supervision through velocity fields constructed from the student's sampling process. Building on this perspective, we introduce Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD), which uses a learned critic to compare student and teacher fields and turn their disagreement into feedback for learning. VAD unifies score distillation, Fisher-based matching, and moment matching, also explaining existing heuristic MMD updates and delivering new training objectives. We further develop VA-TDM, which follows trajectory distribution matching: providing supervision for partial denoising along the student trajectory. Beyond this, VA-TDM combines transition-aware online velocity learning and dual-form VAD supervision across intermediate student transitions. Extensive results show that VA-TDM is powerful for learning few-step generators, achieving state-of-the-art four-step performance in both text-to-image and text-to-video generation across various backbones and scaling effectively to 33B MiniMax-H3. In particular, our VA-TDM-H3 notably outperforms the few-step Fast-H3 and is closer to the original many-step H3 according to human preference.
blocks.zh: 很少分步骤的蒸馏能够有效生成扩散和流动模型,但只有几个取样步骤才能保持质量仍然是挑战。 通过分数蒸馏进行分配比对的方法提供了一个坚实的基础,但它们依赖于准确跟踪学生不断变化的分布. 在几步抽样的中间生成步骤中,学生分数估计可能比较困难,常用的估测器可能描述出不同于用来更新学生的分布. 流量匹配使得通过学生的采样过程构建的速度场,可以更灵活地进行监督. 基于这个观点,我们引入了"极速加速"(Velocity Adversarial Distillation,VAD),它利用一位有学问的批评家来比较学生和教师的领域,把他们的分歧转化为学习的反馈. VAD统一分数衍射,基于费舍尔的比对,以及瞬间比对,也解释现有的Heuristic MMD更新,并交付新的培训目标. 我们进一步发展了VA-TDM,它遵循了轨迹分布的匹配:对沿学生轨迹的部分去名进行监督. 除此之外,VA-TDM将过渡感在线速度学习和跨中学生过渡的双形式VAD监督结合起来. 广泛结果显示,VA-TDM对学习几步生成器,在文本到图像和文本到视频的生成中实现最新四步的性能,并有效放大到33B MiniMax-H3,具有强大的影响力. 特别是,我们的VA-TDM-H3明显优于几步快速H3,并且根据人类的偏好更接近最初的多步H3.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Few-step distillation seeks to make diffusion and flow models efficient without sacrificing generation quality ( Ho et al., 2020 ; Esser et al., 2024 ) . A central challenge is to provide effective supervision when a small number of student transitions must replace a long teacher trajectory. Trajectory distillation learns from individual teacher trajectories ( Song et al., 2023 ) , whereas distribution matching allows the student to learn its own mapping by aligning student and teacher distributions ( Luo et al., 2023 ; Yin et al., 2023 ) . Trajectory Distribution Matching (TDM) ( Luo et al., 2025 ) extends this principle to intermediate transitions. Each step then learns a partial denoising task, distributing supervision across the student trajectory and providing a natural foundation for few-step distillation.
blocks.zh: 很少一步的蒸馏寻求在不牺牲生成质量的情况下使扩散和流出模型高效(Ho等,2020;Esser等,2024.). 一个中心挑战是,当少数学生的过渡必须取代长期的教师轨迹时,提供有效的监督。 轨迹分馏学从个别教师的轨迹中学习(Song等,2023年),而分布比对则让学生通过校正学生和教师分布来学习自己的绘图(Luo等,2023年;Yin等,2023年). 轨迹分布匹配(TDM)(Luo等,2025年)将这一原则延伸至中间过渡. 每一步然后学习部分去名任务,在学生的轨道上分配监督,为几步分馏提供自然的基础.

blocks.en:
For intermediate supervision to be effective, however, the training signal must faithfully reflect the distribution produced at each student step. In score-based methods, generator updates depend on the difference between teacher and student scores, requiring an auxiliary model to track the evolving student distribution. Intermediate transitions complicate this estimation: the student’s clean prediction and retained residual can be correlated, so perturbing its intermediate output generally differs from adding fresh Gaussian noise to the clean prediction.
Our analysis of TDM shows why this distinction matters. Direct score estimation for the perturbed intermediate output can involve high-variance targets, while clean-target denoising can estimate a different distribution from the one used for generator supervision.
blocks.zh:
然而,要使中级监督有效,培训信号必须忠实地反映每个学生阶段产生的分布。 在以分数为基础的方法中,生成器更新取决于师生分数的差异,需要辅助模型来跟踪不断发展的学生分布. 中间过渡使这一估计复杂化:学生的清洁预测和所保留的残留可以相互关联,因此干扰其中间输出一般不同于在清洁预测中添加新鲜高斯噪音.
我们对TDM的分析表明,这一区别为何重要。 对扰动中间产物的直接分数估计可能涉及高变异目标,而清洁目标去诺能估计出与用于发电机监理的分布不同.

blocks.en:
These observations motivate supervision that explicitly accounts for the student’s sampling process while allowing alternatives to its noisy-marginal score. Velocity targets offer this flexibility because they can be defined through paths with coupled endpoints ( Liu et al., 2022 ) , including dependencies inherited from a student transition. We build on this flexibility to introduce Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD), a framework for constructing student velocity fields and using their discrepancies from the teacher to guide distillation.
Two prototypical velocity constructions are derived within VAD. A-form is a rectified velocity that captures the expected clean prediction conditioned on a perturbed sample; B-form is a score-equivalent Gaussian velocity for the student’s perturbed distribution. The two forms thus express conditional-moment and distributional supervision within the same sampling process. A vector-valued critic estimates the discrepancy between the chosen student field and the teacher field, and the generator learns from this discrepancy.
blocks.zh:
这些观察促使监督明确说明学生的取样过程,同时允许替代噪音-边际分数。 速度目标提供了这种灵活性,因为它们可以通过附带终点的路径加以界定(Liu等,2022年),包括从学生过渡中继承的依赖性。 我们利用这种灵活性,引入了 " 速度加速 " (VAD),这是一个构建学生速度场并利用他们与教师的差异来指导蒸馏的框架。
在VAD内部衍生出两种原生的速度构造. A-form是一种修正的速度,它能捕捉到在扰动样品上设定的预期清洁预测条件;B-form是学生扰动分布的等分高斯速度. 因此,这两种形式在同一个取样过程中都明确了有条件的移动和分配监督。 一个矢量值的批评家估计了所选择的学生领域和老师领域之间的差异,生成者从这一差异中学习.

blocks.en: The resulting framework provides a unified perspective along two axes: which field to match and how to use its discrepancy to update the generator . With different generator updates, A-form connects to conditional moment matching, while B-form connects reverse-KL score distillation and Fisher-based field matching. These connections also clarify the relationship between an intended objective and its practical update. In particular, VAD explains the heuristic update of MMD ( Salimans et al., 2024 ) and derives an alternative surrogate that recovers the exact gradient of MMD’s desired objective.
blocks.zh: 由此形成的框架沿着两个轴线提供了统一的观点:哪个字段匹配,以及如何利用它的差异来更新生成器 . 随着不同的生成器更新,A-form连接到有条件的瞬间匹配,而B-form连接到倒向-KL分数分馏和以费舍尔为基础的场相匹配. 这些联系还澄清了预期目标与其实际更新之间的关系。 VAD特别解释了MMD(Salimans等人,2024年)的热度更新,并得出了一种替代物,可以恢复MMD期望目标的确切梯度.

To use both types of supervision along a few-step trajectory, we develop VA-TDM , retaining TDM’s supervision of intermediate transitions. VA-TDM combines A-form and B-form through a shared auxiliary backbone and blends complementary generator updates. Because samples from different student steps can follow different distributions even at the same noise level, we also condition field estimation on the transition being supervised.
This provides different and accurate supervision signals among different steps.
blocks.zh:
为了使用两种类型的监督,我们发展了VA-TDM,保留了TDM对中间过渡的监督。 VA-TDM通过共享的辅助骨干将A-形式和B-形式结合,并混合互补的生成器更新. 由于来自不同学生步骤的样本即使在同一噪音水平上也会跟随不同的分布,因此我们也以所监督的过渡为条件进行实地估计.
这在不同步骤之间提供了不同而准确的监督信号.

blocks.en:
Overall, our unified VAD framework connects existing distillation updates and
derives new objectives, which VA-TDM combines with complementary velocity
fields and transition-aware estimation for four-step generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance across backbones and tasks.
On SD3.5-Medium, VA-TDM outperforms the compared few-step baselines across
prompt following, image quality, and preference metrics, improving
GenEval from TDM’s 0.61 to 0.67 while increasing sample diversity.
On FLUX.2-Klein-Base 4B, it surpasses the released four-step model,
raising GenEval from 0.78 to 0.80 and OCR similarity from 0.64 to 0.69,
with diversity measured by LPIPS improving from 0.47 to 0.56.
Most notably, VA-TDM scales to MiniMax-H3 ( MiniMax, 2026 ) ,
a state-of-the-art open-source audio-video model with
33B parameters. In our user study ( Fig. 1 ),
VA-TDM wins 61.33% of comparisons against Fast-H3 at the same 4-NFE
budget and achieves a 45.53% preference rate against the 100-NFE
teacher, compared with 24.67% for Fast-H3.
These results demonstrate that VA-TDM substantially narrows the
perceptual quality gap to the teacher while requiring only
4-NFE.

MMD: Objective and Approximate Update. MMD ( Salimans et al., 2024 ) aims to minimize a squared conditional-moment discrepancy to align the teacher moment and student moment. Because
differentiating the student’s implicit moment is intractable,

objective’s exact gradient under MMD’s fixed-outer-measure convention,
while A-form pathwise updates with a detached critic recover the surrogate
update as a generator update in the adversarial velocity game, up to
positive time weighting on the same sampling chain. Sec. A.4 explicitly gives the target objective,
the approximation leading to the surrogate, and both gradient identities.

blocks.en: Dual-Form Velocity Game with a Shared Backbone. The A-form produces low-variance online field learning, but it only captures the conditional-mean moment of the distribution; the B-form induces high-variance online field learning, yet it encodes the full distributional information. Since no single velocity construction enjoys both benefits, we propose to optimize the adversarial games induced by the two velocity constructions simultaneously, the generator loss becomes: ℒ mix = λ m ​ ℒ mix A + ( 1 − λ m ) ​ ℒ mix B , \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{mix}}=\lambda_{m}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{mix}}^{A}+(1-\lambda_{m})\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{mix}}^{B}, (22) where each term follows Eq. 20 with its corresponding velocity target. To avoid the cost of maintaining two online fields, we propose a shared-backbone strategy: the two field networks share the backbone with separate output heads. Tab. 2 shows that this sharing strategy not only reduces memory and training overhead, but also improves performance.

Transition-Aware Field Estimation. In both our framework and existing score distillation work, it is crucial for the auxiliary score to accurately track the student distribution in order to achieve strong performance. However, we identify an aspect that has been consistently overlooked in prior work ( Yin et al., 2024 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) : in the few-step generation setting, student transitions with different step indices generally induce distinct noisy distributions, yet existing methods typically model them with a shared auxiliary score, which theoretically precludes the possibility of precisely tracking the student distribution.
TDM tries to avoid this by assigning student transitions with different step indices to disjoint perturbation intervals, which is partially effective but sacrifices part of supervision signals.
To resolve this issue, we propose that the field network should additionally receive the identity of the transition —for instance, in our setting, the target timestep of the student transition can be injected as extra input, i.e., learn h ψ ​ ( 𝐱 τ , τ , s ) h_{\psi}(\mathbf{x}_{\tau},\tau,s) as online velocity. Results in Tab. 2 show that this modification is essential for providing accurate supervision signals, and substantially improves diversity and fine-grained rendering of images, such as text rendering.

blocks.en: Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration. Training-free methods for accelerating diffusion model sampling have progressed substantially ( Lu et al., 2022 ; Zhao et al., 2023 ; Xue et al., 2024 ; Si et al., 2024 ; Ma et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025 ) . However, diffusion distillation remains essential for high-quality few-step generation.
blocks.zh: 培训-免费传播加速。 加快扩散模型取样的无培训方法已取得重大进展(Lu等,2022;Zhao等,2023;Xue等,2024;Si等,2024;Ma等,2024;Li等,2025)。 然而,传播蒸馏仍然是高质量几步生成的关键。

blocks.en:
Diffusion Distillation. Distilled models generate images from noise in one or a few steps. Two main approaches transfer knowledge from pre-trained DMs:
1) Trajectory distillation ( Luhman and Luhman, 2021 ; Meng et al., 2023 ; Salimans and Ho, 2022 ; Song et al., 2023 ; Song and Dhariwal, 2024 ; Yan et al., 2024 ) matches teacher ODE trajectories at the instance level, facing challenging instance-wise alignment and numerical errors in teacher PF-ODE solutions;
2) Distribution matching via score distillation ( Yin et al., 2023 ; Luo et al., 2023 ; Zhou et al., 2024b ; Zhou et al., 2024a ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ) aligns student and teacher distributions using objectives such as reverse KL, Fisher divergence, and moment matching.
FGM aligns velocity fields but considers only Gaussian forward processes ( Huang et al., 2024 ) , where its objective reduces to Fisher divergence ( Zhou et al., 2024b ) . TDM ( Luo et al., 2025 ) has shown strong few-step performance by learning partial denoising at each step.
Our VA-TDM unifies score distillation, Fisher divergence, and moment matching while yielding new distillation objectives. Combined with transition-aware online field learning, it achieves state-of-the-art few-step performance.

blocks.en: Generative adversarial networks.. Early GAN research achieved strong results on domain-specific datasets ( Reed et al., 2016 ; Zhang et al., 2017 ; Karras et al., 2020 ; Karras et al., 2021 ) , while it has been effectively extended these successes to ImageNet ( Brock et al., 2019 ; Sauer et al., 2022 ; Russakovsky et al., 2015 ) . However, training instability and limited scalability remain key challenges. Large-scale text-to-image GANs still rely on convolutional architectures with complex designs ( Kang et al., 2023 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) , and scaling transformer-based GANs remains difficult ( Jiang et al., 2021 ; Lee et al., 2021 ) . Adversarial Flow Models (AFM) ( Lin et al., 2026 ) train many-step flow-matching models through an adversarial game in velocity space, requiring discriminator Jacobian-vector products (JVPs). Our work also formulates an adversarial game in velocity space, but targets few-step distillation and avoids expensive JVP computation.
blocks.zh: 基因对抗网络... 早期的GAN研究在域特有数据集上取得了强效成果(Reed等,2016;Zhang等,2017;Karras等,2020;Karras等,2021),而已经有效地将这些成功推广到ImageNet(Brock等,2019;Sauer等,2022;Russakovsky等,2015). 然而,培训不稳定和规模有限仍然是主要挑战。 大规模文本到图像GANs仍然依赖于具有复杂设计的回旋式建筑(Kang等,2023;Zhu等,2025;而以变压器为主的GANs仍然困难(Jiang等,2021;Lee等,2021). 逆流模型(AFM)(Lin等,2026年)通过速度空间的对战游戏来训练多步相流模型,需要歧视者雅各比克活佛的产品(JVPs). 我们的工作还在速度空间中设计出一款对抗游戏,但目标为几步分馏并避免昂贵的JVP计算.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusions
blocks.zh: 6. 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced Velocity Adversarial Distillation (VAD), a unified framework that guides distillation through velocity fields constructed from the student’s sampling process.
By separating the choice of field from the generator update, VAD connects score distillation, Fisher-based matching, and moment matching, clarifies MMD’s heuristic updates, and derives new training objectives.
Building on this framework, VA-TDM combines dual-form supervision with transition-aware online velocity learning to supervise partial denoising along few-step student trajectories, without adding inference cost. Experiments across text-to-image and text-to-video generation demonstrate VA-TDM consistently achieves state-of-the-art four-step performance. VA-TDM also scales effectively to 33B MiniMax-H3, outperforming Fast-H3 in human evaluation and substantially narrowing the perceptual quality gap to the many-step teacher. These results highlight the value of our work, establishing VAD as a principled foundation for designing effective few-step distillation methods.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了极速加速蒸馏(VAD)这个统一框架,通过学生的取样过程构建的速度场指导蒸馏。
通过将字段的选择与生成器更新区分开来,VAD连接了分数分馏,基于费舍尔的匹配,以及瞬间匹配,澄清了MMD的热度更新,并得出了新的培训目标.
以此框架为基础,VA-TDM将双形式监督与过渡意识在线速度学习相结合,监督部分沿少数步骤的学生轨迹去除,而不会增加推论成本. 跨文本到图像和文本到视频生成的实验显示,VA-TDM持续实现最先进的四步性能. VA-TDM还有效地将规模扩大到33B MiniMax-H3,在人类评价方面表现优于快H3,并大大缩小了对多步骤教师的认知质量差距。 这些成果突出表明了我们工作的价值,为设计有效的几步蒸馏方法奠定了一个原则性的基础。

blocks.en: C.2 User Study

blocks.en:
The study in Fig. 1 compares MiniMax-H3 with Fast-H3,
VA-TDM with MiniMax-H3, and VA-TDM with Fast-H3. We carried out a user study in which participants were shown two anonymized audio-videos, each produced by a different model, and were asked to pick the one with superior audio-visual quality and closer alignment with the prompt. For audio-video generation, we randomly chose 10 prompts, and every generated audio-video was manually checked to confirm it contained no inappropriate or harmful content.
